issues.claim: enables lists only W2 and W1 as future consumers of Molt.SyncInductionData's abstracted hStep interface.
issues.actual: W3a.json (docs/rollout/designs/W3a.json, new_theorems 'Molt.sync_rule_mem_timed', Molt/ClientRule.lean:284 line reference reused there too) produces a theorem that 'mirrors' sync_rule_mem exactly, 'called with hBudget replaced by budget_of_reaction; every other argument passed through unchanged' -- i.e. the same membership-shaped per-sync conclusion sync_rule_mem has, just with a derived budget hypothesis. This is a natural additional discharge for SyncInductionData.hStep (a timed-presentation instantiation), directly analogous to the already-listed W1 (mode-3 lockstep) and W2 (certificate level) entries, but W3a is never mentioned in W4's depends_on or enables.
issues.fix: Add a third enables entry for W3a, mirroring the existing W1 entry's wording ('SyncInductionData is crypto/protocol-generic ... a timed mode-1 presentation via W3a's sync_rule_mem_timed could reuse the same structure and .invariant verbatim'). Purely a documentation/completeness gap -- SyncInductionData's own genericity already accommodates this with zero change, so it does not affect implementability or ordering.

issues.claim: goal_statement and the sync_induction_full_chain proof_sketch both state '21 explicit arguments' for the call to Molt.sync_rule_mem.
issues.actual: Molt/ClientRule.lean:284-303 (read directly against the pinned v4.30.0-rc2 toolchain) shows sync_rule_mem takes 22 explicit hypotheses (hn, hEUF, hHash, hVPrev, hTipPrev, hRecPrev, hLongPrev, hAnchor, hCadence, hA, hA', hBudget, hVal, hVal', hTipS, hTipS', hRecent, hRecent', hLong, hLong', hLe, hB) and the design's own binder-mapping list in new_theorems enumerates all 22 of them. The '21' figure appearing twice in the prose is an off-by-one miscount of the design's own correct, fully-enumerated argument list.
issues.fix: Change '21 explicit arguments' to '22 explicit arguments' in both the goal_statement and the sync_induction_full_chain proof_sketch. Cosmetic only -- the actual enumerated call list is correct and matches the live source verbatim, so this does not affect implementability.

issues.claim: (fleet-wide context, not a W4-authored defect) touches_existing entries across the batch are all minimal, single-purpose import-line additions with no cross-item interference implied.
issues.actual: W2.json and W3a.json both specify their new Molt.lean import line at the identical insertion point ('after import Molt.MaxSync', W3a additionally pinning 'before import Molt.Liveness'). If both land, whichever implements second will find the anchor line no longer immediately precedes MaxSync's neighbor as described. This does not involve W4: W4's own anchor ('after Molt.ClientRule, before Molt.MaxSync') is unique among all six sibling designs' touches_existing entries, confirmed by reading every other design's Molt.lean touch. Lean import order carries no compilation semantics here (all modules resolve independently of listed order), so the collision is cosmetic and self-resolving without redesign of either W2 or W3a.
issues.fix: No action needed for W4. Worth a one-line heads-up to whoever sequences W2/W3a landings so the second implementer just appends adjacent to the first rather than being surprised the described anchor line moved.

confirmed_reuses: Molt.sync_rule_mem exists exactly as cited at Molt/ClientRule.lean:284, with the 22-hypothesis signature and ∃ i', i' + n < len ∧ blockAt? sc' i' = some B conclusion shape the design describes; read directly from source.
List.mem_of_getElem? confirmed at Init/Data/List/Lemmas.lean:479 in the pinned leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2 toolchain (exact line match against the design's citation).
List.IsPrefix.mem confirmed at Init/Data/List/Sublist.lean:816 in the same pinned toolchain (exact line match, not deprecated/protected).

Molt.lean's current import order (Protocol, Verifier, Assumptions, Results, Rotation, ClientRule, MaxSync, Liveness, Axioms) matches the design's described anchors exactly; the two proposed insertion points ('after ClientRule, before MaxSync' and 'after Axioms') are valid, minimal, and add nothing beyond two import lines -- no edit to any existing declaration, no new field on any existing structure.

Molt/Axioms.lean's existing top-level (no-namespace), one-#guard_msgs-per-theorem format is confirmed by direct read and matches the design's AxiomsSyncInduction.lean layout plan; this 'new guard file per item' idiom (rather than editing Molt/Axioms.lean) is independently used by W2, W3a, W5 and W6's own designs, so W4's approach is not a one-off invention but the batch's established additive pattern.

W2.json's own cert_sync_rule (docs/rollout/designs/W2.json) is confirmed to conclude 'B = B'' (equal-height/equal-index form, mirroring Molt.sync_rule not sync_rule_mem), corroborating W4's depends_on characterization that W2's current design does not yet supply a membership-shaped per-sync lemma and that the W2 dependency is genuinely soft/non-blocking, not something W4 would need redone if W2 lands first or vice versa.

No other design among W1, W2, W3a, W5, W6, W7 defines any declaration named SyncInductionData, sync_induction_full_chain, mem_of_blockAt?, or anything in Molt/SyncInduction.lean / Molt/AxiomsSyncInduction.lean -- confirmed by grepping every design file. No structure-ownership loop risk found.

No change to MoltPetit.lean is required by this item (confirmed: Molt/ClientRule.lean's existing import chain already brings in everything Molt/SyncInduction.lean needs), consistent with the repo idiom that Molt/ imports MoltPetit/ and never the reverse, and that this item is Molt-only.
ordering_notes: W4 stands genuinely independent among the seven sibling items for the purposes it claims: its Molt.lean insertion slot is unique (no sibling targets 'after ClientRule/before MaxSync'), its two new files (Molt/SyncInduction.lean, Molt/AxiomsSyncInduction.lean) are unique paths and unique declaration names against every other design, and its stated 'soft' dependency on W2 is corroborated by W2's own design text (cert_sync_rule is confirmed to be an equal-height form, not yet a membership form, so nothing about W4 would need redoing if W2 lands first, and W2 landing later needs only a new hStep discharge, not a re-touch of SyncInductionData or .invariant). The only gap found is a documentation omission: W3a's sync_rule_mem_timed (a budget-generalised mirror of sync_rule_mem) is exactly the kind of additional hStep discharge the enables section already flags for W1 and W2, but W3a itself is absent from that list -- a one-line addition, not a redesign. A separate, W4-unrelated collision exists between W2 and W3a's identical Molt.lean insertion anchors ('after Molt.MaxSync'); flagged here only as fleet context since Lean import order has no compilation effect and neither item needs redesign over it. Landing order recommendation: W4 can land at any point relative to W1/W2/W3a/W5/W6/W7 with zero rework in either direction; it neither blocks nor is blocked by any of them for its own stated scope.
